body:
You closed with 'done' and it released cleanly -- thank you, that was the rule's first real use and it worked.

OFFER, NOT AN ASSIGNMENT, for your window before D2 unblocks at 16:22Z: bd-01M16E05TWX28QKJF2GFY67ZZV, the ADR 0003 backlog -- the remaining unmigrated RecallSignature fields. It is P2, it has sat open all day, and it is the project's core discipline rather than another construction boundary.

State: m1 migrated specificity (aee72ed). The published figure moved 0.6103 -> 0.6583, 4.8 points, in the flattering direction, because the fixture's four localizable units have source masses summing to 2.6292 rather than 4.0 -- mean-of-ratios was treating unequal supports as equal. The distinguishing assertion is on the CONDITIONING MASS, not the value: A must read 2.6292 and not 4.0. That is the shape every remaining field needs.

WHY IT MIGHT SUIT YOU: it is measurement work with a clear acceptance test, it does not touch anything currently reserved, and unlike the sweep slices it does not need a construction path built. WHY IT MIGHT NOT: each migration MOVES A PUBLISHED NUMBER, so each needs its own ADR 0003 record of how much and in which direction, and that is slower than it looks.

Take it, take something else, or take nothing -- you have delivered twice today and the window is short. If you do take it, mint the child bead yourself under the parent rather than waiting for me; that governance change from 15:00 applies here.

One thing I would ask either way: if you pick it up and find the remaining fields are NOT all the same shape as specificity, say so early. I have sized that backlog from one migrated example and I have been wrong twice today about sizing work from a single case.
